entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.summary: Ask SMA-819 session to add Anthropic order bug
input.message:
For the session that works on SMA-819 (Anthropic translator) only. If you do not work on SMA-819, ignore this message.

Sven asked me (the SMA-810 session) to tell you: include a second Anthropic translator bug in SMA-819.

The bug: in crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs, the Item::AssistantMessage arm calls flush_pending_user BEFORE flush_pending_assistant. A ToolCall that comes after a UserMessage goes to pending_tool_use (the last message is not an assistant message). So the items [User, ToolCall, ToolResult, AssistantMessage] become: user, user[tool_result], assistant[tool_use], assistant[text]. The tool_result comes before its tool_use, and Anthropic rejects this. This shape occurs on every later run of a session after a tool-only model response (the session history replays it). The same arms also have related problems:
- [User, TC a, TR a, TC b, TR b, AM]: TC b also goes to pending_tool_use, so two rounds join into one assistant message.
- [AM, TC a, TR a, TC b]: TC b is appended to the earlier assistant message while the result of a is still pending.

Found by the SMA-810 spec challenge and confirmed by reading the code. I did not run a test. Please verify the wire format with a container (Sven's rule for provider wire formats). A fix should keep each round in order: assistant[tool_use...], then user[tool_result...], then the next item.

SMA-810 does not change this file. SMA-810 changes core: a handoff transfer call now gets its ToolOutputItem directly after HandoffItem, and project() repairs old sessions. So the next run of a handoff session has exactly the [User, TC, TR, AM] shape.

For the session that works on SMA-819 (Anthropic translator) only. If you do not work on SMA-819, ignore this message.

Sven asked me (the SMA-810 session) to tell you: include a second Anthropic translator bug in SMA-819.

The bug: in crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs, the Item::AssistantMessage arm calls flush_pending_user BEFORE flush_pending_assistant. A ToolCall that comes after a UserMessage goes to pending_tool_use (the last message is not an assistant message). So the items [User, ToolCall, ToolResult, AssistantMessage] become: user, user[tool_result], assistant[tool_use], assistant[text]. The tool_result comes before its tool_use, and Anthropic rejects this. This shape occurs on every later run of a session after a tool-only model response (the session history replays it). The same arms also have related problems:
- [User, TC a, TR a, TC b, TR b, AM]: TC b also goes to pending_tool_use, so two rounds join into one assistant message.
- [AM, TC a, TR a, TC b]: TC b is appended to the earlier assistant message while the result of a is still pending.

Found by the SMA-810 spec challenge and confirmed by reading the code. I did not run a test. Please verify the wire format with a container (Sven's rule for provider wire formats). A fix should keep each round in order: assistant[tool_use...], then user[tool_result...], then the next item.

SMA-810 does not change this file. SMA-810 changes core: a handoff transfer call now gets its ToolOutputItem directly after HandoffItem, and project() repairs old sessions. So the next run of a handoff session has exactly the [User, TC, TR, AM] shape.

patch.text:
## Part 2: tool result name for a repeated call id

Added on 2026-11-20 from the SMA-810 spec challenge.

The translator finds the name of a `functionResponse` by call id. It builds one `call_id -> name` map over all items before it translates (`items_to_contents` in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`). The last call with an id wins. Gemini makes the fallback ids `fc_{n}` per stream, so two calls in one conversation can have the same id. Then an earlier tool result gets the tool name of a later call.

Example: turn 1 calls `search` with id `fc_0`, turn 2 calls `pay` with id `fc_0`. The `functionResponse` of `search` is sent with the name `pay`.

This occurs in any multi-turn Gemini conversation with a repeated id. SMA-810 makes it more frequent: a handoff child can now defer a call whose id repeats the transfer call id.

### Required behavior (part 2)

* A tool result gets the name of its own call: the most recent earlier `ToolCall` (or `ContentPart::ToolUse`) with the same id that has no result yet.

### Acceptance criteria (part 2)

* A unit test with two calls that share `fc_0` and have different names asserts the correct name on each `functionResponse`.
* The live check (or keyless proxy container) shows whether Gemini rejects a `functionResponse` whose name does not match its `functionCall`, before and after the fix.

{"id":"SMA-820","uuid":"c211602b-e548-4b8a-ba1b-1f166d3cd273","title":"Gemini translator sends two adjacent user contents after a tool result","description":"The Gemini translator maps a tool result to a `role: user` content with a `functionResponse` part. When a user message comes directly after the tool result, the translator sends a second `role: user` content. The request then has two `role: user` contents next to each other.

No official source says whether the Gemini API accepts this. If the API rejects it or handles it badly, the run fails at the next model call.

Two paths cause this shape:

* A turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject(..)` after a tool turn (PR #346).
* A resumed run after a deferred tool call. This shape is on `main` before PR #346.

## Required behavior

* The translator merges adjacent contents that have the same role into one content, and keeps the order of the parts.
* The rule applies to every message, so replayed session items are also covered.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live check against the Gemini API (or a keyless proxy container) shows how the API handles two adjacent `role: user` contents, before and after the fix.
* The Gemini `request.rs` test that pins the tool-result-then-user-message shape changes to assert one merged `role: user` content.
* A new test covers a merge of more than two adjacent contents with the same role.

## Part 2: tool result name for a repeated call id

Added on 2026-11-20 from the <issue id="25885f3b-a366-4df6-bb75-6e2683c4b0ab" label="SMA-810" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-810/handoff-transfer-call-has-no-tool-result-so-the-stored-session-gets-a" /> spec challenge.

The translator finds the name of a `functionResponse` by call id. It builds one `call_id -> name` map over all items before it translates (`items_to_contents` in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`). The last call with an id wins.   The reworked G4 is correct for every sequential log that I traced. Its target position is valid for all in-scope translators. G5 is correct for sequential streams, but its `TurnStarted` reset makes `ParallelAgent` output worse than today, and the spec's own test oracle cannot pass on a correct G5. T10 and T14 have gaps that let wrong implementations pass. I found no blocker.
  
  ## Findings
  
  ### BLOCKER
  None
  
  ### MAJOR
  - **G5 reset at `TurnStarted` regresses `ParallelAgent` for all providers** - `ParallelAgent` forwards branch events through `select_all` (`workflow.rs:377-420`, `other => yield other`). So branch B's `TurnStarted` can arrive between branch A's deltas and A's `ToolCallItem`.
    - **Today:** `close_call` only ends A's span. `call_names` and `completed_calls` stay. A's later deltas reopen under the same id with the same name. A's `ToolCallItem` hits the `completed_calls` arm (`map.rs:226-231`) and renders nothing.
    - **With G5:** the reset clears all three tables. A's next delta becomes a new call `call_a~2` with name `"unknown"`, because continuation deltas carry `name: None` (`map.rs:172-188`, `name_of` `map.rs:388-392`). If B's `TurnStarted` comes after A's last delta, A's `ToolCallItem` falls to the synthesize arm (`map.rs:232-241`) and emits a second complete call.
    - This also happens with OpenAI and Anthropic ids, which never repeat. The spec says "this is the same limit as today" (spec 243-245). That is not correct.
    - | Why it matters: a setup that works today with unique-id providers starts to show duplicate calls or "unknown" calls. The change only fixes a Gemini problem.
    - | Suggested fix: do not tie the reset to `TurnStarted`. Start a new occurrence of a provider id per call:
      - when a `ToolCallDelta` with `name: Some` arrives for an id that already has a name (core contract: `name` is `Some` exactly once per call, `model.rs:183-206`, which the mapper already relies on at `map.rs:81-86`);
      - when a `ToolCallItem` arrives for an id whose item the mapper already saw.
  
      A `ToolOutputItem` then uses the alias of the latest occurrence. If you keep the `TurnStarted` rule, correct the limit text and add a T14 case that records the new `ParallelAgent` output.
  - **`assert_tool_calls_well_formed` cannot hold on a correct G5** - Check (3) keys `received` on the provider `call_id` of each `ToolCallDelta`, and `emitted` on the AG-UI `toolCallId` (`map.rs:634-661`). Take the T14 case "turn 1 `fc_0`, turn 2 `fc_0`". `received["fc_0"]` holds the args of both calls, but `emitted["fc_0"]` holds only the first call's args, so the assert fails. The spec says only "Update the docs for the alias rule" (spec 241-242), and T14 says the assert "holds on every case" (spec 391). | Why it matters: the builder must invent the oracle change. An oracle that copies the mapper's alias logic passes a wrong mapper. | Suggested fix: specify the oracle in the spec. Split `received` per call occurrence with an independent rule (for example, cut at each `TurnStarted` in the sequential fixtures), and map occurrence n of id x to `x` or `x~n`. Also assert that each `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` uses the AG-UI id of the call that its `ToolOutputItem` closes.

The most common handoff is a tool-only transfer response followed by child text.
    - **Today:** the old layout projects to `user, TC t, AM(child), TR t`. This translates to `user, assistant[tool_use t], assistant[text], user[tool_result t]`. The API probably accepts it, if it merges consecutive same-role turns.

    - I did not check either shape against the live API.
    - | Why it matters: if the old shape is accepted, SMA-810 turns working Anthropic handoff sessions (old and new) into failing ones until SMA-819 is on crates.io. The spec says "SMA-810 needs no change", but it gives no release order.
    - | Suggested fix: do a live check of both shapes. If the old shape is accepted, state in "Release and docs" that SMA-819 ships first or in the same release, and say so in the PR body.
  - **T10 does not lock the AG1 boundary of the text rewrite** - Step 5 rewrites only a moved cancel result (spec 179-186). Only this rule keeps a false "transferred" text out of an old log where the target never started. The old code yields `HandoffItem` before `target_agent.run()` (`agent.rs:1674-1692`). So a failed `run()` gives `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`, with the result already adjacent.
    - T10 has no case for this.
    - T10 has no case where a child call that was running at the cancel keeps its own cancel text.
    - The three-level case does not check that each level gets the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.
    - | Why it matters: an implementation that rewrites every cancel result after a `HandoffOccurred`, or that uses one `to` for all levels, passes T10 and breaks AG1 at read time.
    - | Suggested fix: add three cases:
      - (a) `user, TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)` projects unchanged, with the cancel text;
      - (b) `TC fc_0(T), HO, TC fc_0(C), cancel, cancel` gives `transferred to …` to T and the cancel text to C;
      - (c) the three-level case asserts `transferred to budgeting` and `transferred to savings` at their own positions.

  - **Step 1 can capture a call that is not a transfer call** - The scan stops only at an event that is not `ToolCalled` or `AssistantMessage` (`deferral.rs:650-660`). Two cases put another call into that run of events:
    - a `ParallelAgent` sibling's `ToolCalled` between the branch's `ToolCallItem` and its `HandoffItem`. The `OnHandoff` await (`agent.rs:1656-1661`) is a yield point.
    - a non-resume run whose input ends with a `ToolCall`. That input is recorded with no check (`runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:129-133`).
  
    Step 5 can then write "transferred …" or "transfer not performed …" on a normal call. Under `ParallelAgent`, sibling events after `HandoffOccurred` also cause a move when `run()` failed, so "transferred" is false there.

(SequentialAgent stops on a failure, `workflow.rs:226-231`, so only `ParallelAgent` breaks this.)

    - An old log where `run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new layout gives `transfer failed: …`.
    - An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event also keeps "did not complete". The model can still call the transfer tool again in that case.

    - Every core version before SMA-810 writes the old layout, not only 0.6.0.
    - Fix: list these exceptions, and say "sessions stored before SMA-810".

  - **O(n) claim versus the shared helper** - `transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward scan for each transfer call (`deferral.rs:666-671`). If `project()` calls this helper unchanged, `project()` becomes O(n × transfer calls). It runs on every snapshot and on every `CompactingSession::append` (`compacting_session.rs:147`, `181`). Fix: share only the boundary scan.
  - **"neither changes" for `CompactingSession`** (spec 192-193) - The rewrite changes the text length, so the token estimate changes slightly. This is harmless, but tests must not assert equal token counts.
  - **The `close_open_transfers` move branch loses its test coverage** - After G4, `MemorySession` snapshots are already repaired. So the four "moves the recorded transfer result" tests (`deferred_resume.rs:1091-1145`, `1235`, `1299`) and T13 still pass if the branch at `resume_exec.rs:182-186` is deleted. Fix: add one test with a custom `Session` whose `snapshot()` does not call `project()`.
  - **T12 wording** - "Change … to the round rule" can be read as "replace". The current oracle also rejects a `UserMessage` or `AssistantMessage` while calls are outstanding (`deferred_resume.rs:598-603`). Without that check, `TC t, AM, TR t` passes, and that request is invalid for OpenAI Chat. Fix: write "add the round rule to the existing checks".
  - **T14 does not test what it names** - In the handoff fixture, the transfer call `fc_1` is the first use of its id, so its AG-UI id is the provider id. A mapper that never puts an alias on a result, or that clears aliases at `HandoffItem`, passes. The fixture streams `search` first, so `search` is the open call, not a buffered call. So the new `TurnStarted` flush, and its order before the `call_names` clear, are not tested. Fix: make the transfer call the second use of its id (`fc_1~2`). Add a case where the transfer delta comes first.
  - **T10 has no case with a `Compacted` event before the handoff** - In real sessions, a compaction happens first and an old-layout handoff run comes after it. Fix: add `user, AM, Compacted(2), user, TC t, HO, AM(child), TR t(cancel)`.
  - **Alias edge cases** - `{id}~{n}` can be equal to a real provider id (`x~2`). The `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame carries the provider `call_id` (`agent.rs:482-489`, `map.rs:286`), so a client cannot connect it to an aliased span. Fix: skip an alias that the run already used. Put the alias in the approval frame, or document the gap.
  
  ### QUESTIONS
  - **AG-UI ids across runs.** The mapper and the session are new for each request (`agui/sse.rs:130`, `187`). Gemini restarts `fc_{n}` in each response (`providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). So two runs in one AG-UI thread both emit `fc_0`, and a client that keys on `toolCallId` still merges them. Is "unique per run" the intended scope? If yes, state it as a G5 limit.
  - **The no-alias result rule.** AgentCore turns Defer into Deny (`invoke.rs:178-192`). So the rule "a result with no alias uses the provider id" can only apply under `ParallelAgent`. Under `ParallelAgent`, that id belongs to the first use, which can be a different call. Is that acceptable?
  - **Removal of the repair.** Does the read-time repair have an end date or a removal condition? If not, put it in its own named function, so that it is clear and easy to test.
  - **Ollama.** The review brief names an Ollama translator, but the workspace has no `providers-ollama` crate. Is a translator missing from the scope list?
  
  ## What's good
  - **G4 now moves only transfer results, to a fixed place.** I traced the step-2 rule on these logs, and each result paired with its true call:
    - a child call with the same id and a real result;
    - a child call that was still running at the cancel;
    - three levels with one id;
    - two handoffs in a row with one id;
    - an old deferral that a new-code resume continues;
    - a handoff directly after a resume.
  
    In sequential logs the scan sees only transfer calls. It stops at the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at the earlier `HandoffOccurred`. Dropped non-transfer calls are never recorded (`loop_state.rs:303-315`). The target position is valid for OpenAI Chat (`request.rs:54-79`), OpenAI Responses (`request.rs:323-341`), LiteLLM (`request.rs:56-81`) and Bedrock (`request.rs:197-219`, which coalesces turns).
  - **The `sources` list keeps `Compacted` on event counts.** `CompactingSession` always compacts all live events (`compacting_session.rs:196-232`). Checkpoints do not write in the middle of a run (`checkpoint.rs:71-73`). So with the shipped code, a `Compacted` event cannot come between a transfer call and its late result. The `agent_view` segments are safe: a segment that ends before a `HandoffOccurred`, or starts after it, never holds both the transfer call and its handoff.
  - **G5's per-stream scope is sound for sequential flows.** Tool results always come before the next `TurnStarted` (`loop_state.rs:467-489`). The transfer result comes before the child's first `TurnStarted`. `agent_as_tool` forwards no child events. G5 also fixes a real bug: today a child's non-streamed call that reuses a parent id is not rendered, because `completed_calls` still holds that id.

  - **After G1 and G4:** the projection is `user, TC t, TR t, AM(child)`. This translates to `user, user[tool_result t], assistant[tool_use t], assistant[text]`. The API rejects that, because the result comes before its call.
  - I did not check either shape against the live API.
  - | Why it matters: if the old shape is accepted, SMA-810 turns working Anthropic handoff sessions (old and new) into failing ones until SMA-819 is on crates.io. The spec says "SMA-810 needs no change", but it gives no release order.
  - | Suggested fix: do a live check of both shapes. If the old shape is accepted, state in "Release and docs" that SMA-819 ships first or in the same release, and say so in the PR body.
- **T10 does not lock the AG1 boundary of the text rewrite** - Step 5 rewrites only a moved cancel result (spec 179-186). Only this rule keeps a false "transferred" text out of an old log where the target never started. The old code yields `HandoffItem` before `target_agent.run()` (`agent.rs:1674-1692`). So a failed `run()` gives `TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)`, with the result already adjacent.
  - T10 has no case for this.
  - T10 has no case where a child call that was running at the cancel keeps its own cancel text.
  - The three-level case does not check that each level gets the `to` of its own `HandoffOccurred`.
  - | Why it matters: an implementation that rewrites every cancel result after a `HandoffOccurred`, or that uses one `to` for all levels, passes T10 and breaks AG1 at read time.
  - | Suggested fix: add three cases:
    - (a) `user, TC t, HO, TR t(cancel)` projects unchanged, with the cancel text;
    - (b) `TC fc_0(T), HO, TC fc_0(C), cancel, cancel` gives `transferred to …` to T and the cancel text to C;
    - (c) the three-level case asserts `transferred to budgeting` and `transferred to savings` at their own positions.

### MINOR
- **Step 1 can capture a call that is not a transfer call** - The scan stops only at an event that is not `ToolCalled` or `AssistantMessage` (`deferral.rs:650-660`). Two cases put another call into that run of events:
  - a `ParallelAgent` sibling's `ToolCalled` between the branch's `ToolCallItem` and its `HandoffItem`. The `OnHandoff` await (`agent.rs:1656-1661`) is a yield point.
  - a non-resume run whose input ends with a `ToolCall`. That input is recorded with no check (`runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:129-133`).

  Step 5 can then write "transferred …" or "transfer not performed …" on a normal call. Under `ParallelAgent`, sibling events after `HandoffOccurred` also cause a move when `run()` failed, so "transferred" is false there.
  - Fix: extend the G3 `ParallelAgent` limit to G4 in the spec. Replace the sentence "The `HandoffOccurred` event proves that the transfer occurred" with the real rule: in a sequential log, a recorded event between `HandoffOccurred` and the late result comes from the target that started. (SequentialAgent stops on a failure, `workflow.rs:226-231`, so only `ParallelAgent` breaks this.)
- **"Projects exactly as a new-layout session" is not exact** (spec 49-50).
  - An old log where `run()` failed keeps the cancel text. The new layout gives `transfer failed: …`.
  - An old successful handoff whose child recorded no event also keeps "did not complete". The model can still call the transfer tool again in that case.
  - Each sequential case that I traced gives a true "transferred" text. This includes a child run that was cancelled.
  - Every core version before SMA-810 writes the old layout, not only 0.6.0.
  - Fix: list these exceptions, and say "sessions stored before SMA-810".
- **The cancel text is a literal** (`session.rs:724-731`) - Step 5 matches it exactly. Fix: use one `const` in `cancelled_result`, in the repair, and in the T7 helper. If the helper writes any other text, T11 does not test step 5.
- **T7 helper position** (spec 342-344) - Core 0.6.0 appends the cancel at the end of the run's batch (`session.rs:695-708`; one `append` per run, `runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs:150-154`), not at the end of the log. Fix: say "at the end of the handoff run's events".
- **O(n) claim versus the shared helper** - `transfer_calls_before` also counts `later_calls` with a forward scan for each transfer call (`deferral.rs:666-671`). If `project()` calls this helper unchanged, `project()` becomes O(n × transfer calls). It runs on every snapshot and on every `CompactingSession::append` (`compacting_session.rs:147`, `181`). Fix: share only the boundary scan.
- **"neither changes" for `CompactingSession`** (spec 192-193) - The rewrite changes the text length, so the token estimate changes slightly. This is harmless, but tests must not assert equal token counts.
- **The `close_open_transfers` move branch loses its test coverage** - After G4, `MemorySession` snapshots are already repaired. So the four "moves the recorded transfer result" tests (`deferred_resume.rs:1091-1145`, `1235`, `1299`) and T13 still pass if the branch at `resume_exec.rs:182-186` is deleted. Fix: add one test with a custom `Session` whose `snapshot()` does not call `project()`.
- **T12 wording** - "Change … to the round rule" can be read as "replace". The current oracle also rejects a `UserMessage` or `AssistantMessage` while calls are outstanding (`deferred_resume.rs:598-603`). Without that check, `TC t, AM, TR t` passes, and that request is invalid for OpenAI Chat. Fix: write "add the round rule to the existing checks".
- **T14 does not test what it names** - In the handoff fixture, the transfer call `fc_1` is the first use of its id, so its AG-UI id is the provider id. A mapper that never puts an alias on a result, or that clears aliases at `HandoffItem`, passes. The fixture streams `search` first, so `search` is the open call, not a buffered call. So the new `TurnStarted` flush, and its order before the `call_names` clear, are not tested. Fix: make the transfer call the second use of its id (`fc_1~2`). Add a case where the transfer delta comes first.
- **T10 has no case with a `Compacted` event before the handoff** - In real sessions, a compaction happens first and an old-layout handoff run comes after it. Fix: add `user, AM, Compacted(2), user, TC t, HO, AM(child), TR t(cancel)`.
- **Alias edge cases** - `{id}~{n}` can be equal to a real provider id (`x~2`). The `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame carries the provider `call_id` (`agent.rs:482-489`, `map.rs:286`), so a client cannot connect it to an aliased span. Fix: skip an alias that the run already used. Put the alias in the approval frame, or document the gap.

### QUESTIONS
- **AG-UI ids across runs.** The mapper and the session are new for each request (`agui/sse.rs:130`, `187`). Gemini restarts `fc_{n}` in each response (`providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:43`). So two runs in one AG-UI thread both emit `fc_0`, and a client that keys on `toolCallId` still merges them. Is "unique per run" the intended scope? If yes, state it as a G5 limit.
- **The no-alias result rule.** AgentCore turns Defer into Deny (`invoke.rs:178-192`). So the rule "a result with no alias uses the provider id" can only apply under `ParallelAgent`. Under `ParallelAgent`, that id belongs to the first use, which can be a different call. Is that acceptable?
- **Removal of the repair.** Does the read-time repair have an end date or a removal condition? If not, put it in its own named function, so that it is clear and easy to test.
- **Ollama.** The review brief names an Ollama translator, but the workspace has no `providers-ollama` crate. Is a translator missing from the scope list?

## What's good
- **G4 now moves only transfer results, to a fixed place.** I traced the step-2 rule on these logs, and each result paired with its true call:
  - a child call with the same id and a real result;
  - a child call that was still running at the cancel;
  - three levels with one id;
  - two handoffs in a row with one id;
  - an old deferral that a new-code resume continues;
  - a handoff directly after a resume.

  In sequential logs the scan sees only transfer calls. It stops at the resume block, at `UserMessageInjected`, at recorded input and at the earlier `HandoffOccurred`. Dropped non-transfer calls are never recorded (`loop_state.rs:303-315`). The target position is valid for OpenAI Chat (`request.rs:54-79`), OpenAI Responses (`request.rs:323-341`), LiteLLM (`request.rs:56-81`) and Bedrock (`request.rs:197-219`, which coalesces turns).
- **The `sources` list keeps `Compacted` on event counts.** `CompactingSession` always compacts all live events (`compacting_session.rs:196-232`). Checkpoints do not write in the middle of a run (`checkpoint.rs:71-73`). So with the shipped code, a `Compacted` event cannot come between a transfer call and its late result. The `agent_view` segments are safe: a segment that ends before a `HandoffOccurred`, or starts after it, never holds both the transfer call and its handoff.
- **G5's per-stream scope is sound for sequential flows.** Tool results always come before the next `TurnStarted` (`loop_state.rs:467-489`). The transfer result comes before the child's first `TurnStarted`. `agent_as_tool` forwards no child events. G5 also fixes a real bug: today a child's non-streamed call that reuses a parent id is not rendered, because `completed_calls` still holds that id.

  conversation (the model request), not in the raw log.
- G4. **Read-time repair of old sessions** (added at Gate 1 on Sven's request).
  `project()` moves the late result of each **transfer call** to directly after the
  transfer calls of its handoff response, and replaces the synthetic cancel text with
  the transfer text. A session that core 0.6.0 stored then projects exactly as a
  new-layout session. Every session backend (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis) builds
  its snapshot with `core::project`, so the repair covers all of them. The stored log
  does not change. No other result moves.
- G5. **AG-UI call state per model stream, and one AG-UI id per call** (added at Gate 1
  on Sven's request). The AG-UI `EventMapper` keys `call_names`, `completed_calls` and
  `buffered_calls` by call id for the whole run. A provider that repeats call ids across
  model streams (Gemini `fc_{n}`) then gets a wrong tool name, a missing call, or merged
  arguments. Also, a client that keys on `toolCallId` merges two calls with one id. The
  mapper must scope call state to one model stream and give each call its own AG-UI id.

- The stored log of an old session does not change. G4 repairs only the projection.

content.content:
140	(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
141	LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
142	in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
143	results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.
144	
145	**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
146	transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
147	`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
148	`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`); the two places use one shared private helper.
149	
150	**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
151	the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
152	with call id `x` closes:
153	
154	1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
155	2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.
156	
157	Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
158	The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,
159	`TR fc_0 (child)`, …, `TR fc_0 (late cancel)`. The rule gives the child's result to
160	the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
161	non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.
162	
163	**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list
164	`sources` with the event index of each message. `Compacted` truncates `sources` with
165	`messages`. (A `Compacted` event counts **events**, so the repair must not reorder
166	events before projection: that would change which events a later `Compacted` removes.)
167	
168	**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
169	still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call
170	message of that response. Each transfer result that is in `messages` but not at its
171	target moves there, in the order of its call. In one O(n) rebuild pass (no repeated
172	`Vec::remove`/`insert`):
173	
174	- A result that is already at its target (the new layout) does not move.
175	- A result whose call was removed by `Compacted` stays where it is (today's behaviour).
176	- A result removed by `Compacted` while its call stays: the call keeps no result, as
177	  today.
178	
179	**Step 5: correct the text of a moved late result.** If a moved result has exactly
180	the synthetic cancel text (`tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)`), the
181	repair replaces it with the G1 text: `transferred to {to}` for the first transfer call
182	of the response (`to` comes from the `HandoffOccurred` event), and `transfer not
183	performed: this response already transferred to {to}` for each other call. The
184	`HandoffOccurred` event proves that the transfer occurred, so the cancel text is false.
185	Without this step, the model sees "did not complete" after a transfer that succeeded,
186	and it can call the transfer tool again. A result with any other text keeps its text.
187	
188	Properties:
189	
190	- A log that has no `HandoffOccurred`, and a new-layout log, project exactly as today.
191	  This includes `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids.
192	- The repair adds and removes no message, so the message count stays the same.
193	  (`CompactingSession` counts tokens and checks `len()`; neither changes.)
194	- After the repair, a transfer call and its result are adjacent in the sense of
195	  `close_open_transfers` (result directly after the transfer calls of its response). So
196	  FIFO (`paired_result`, `agent_view`) and the step 2 rule give the same pairs for

(`model.rs` `build_items`), so one block can hold several responses, and the OpenAI and
LiteLLM translators then still send an invalid request. That version also moved results
in `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids, where it could swap the content of two
results. This version moves **only transfer results**, to a fixed place.

**Step 1: find the transfer calls.** For each `HandoffOccurred` at index `k`, the
transfer calls are the `ToolCalled` events in the run of `ToolCalled` /
`AssistantMessage` events directly before `k`. This is the scan of
`transfer_calls_before` (`deferral.rs`); the two places use one shared private helper.

**Step 2: find the result of each transfer call** (one O(n) pass over the events). Keep
the list of open calls, each with a flag "transfer". A `ToolReturned` or `ToolDeferred`
with call id `x` closes:

1. the most recent open **non-transfer** call with id `x`, if one exists;
2. else the earliest open **transfer** call with id `x`.

Why: in the old layout a child call can repeat the transfer call id (Gemini `fc_0`).
The log is then `TC fc_0 (transfer)`, `HandoffOccurred`, `TC fc_0 (child)`,
`TR fc_0 (child)`, …, `TR fc_0 (late cancel)`. The rule gives the child's result to
the child's call and the late cancel to the transfer call. The rule changes nothing for
non-transfer calls, because non-transfer results do not move.

**Step 3: project as today, and keep the source.** `project()` keeps a parallel list
`sources` with the event index of each message. `Compacted` truncates `sources` with
`messages`. (A `Compacted` event counts **events**, so the repair must not reorder
events before projection: that would change which events a later `Compacted` removes.)

**Step 4: move, after projection.** For each handoff response whose transfer calls are
still in `messages`: the target position is directly after the last transfer call
message of that response. Each transfer result that is in `messages` but not at its
target moves there, in the order of its call. In one O(n) rebuild pass (no repeated
`Vec::remove`/`insert`):

- A result that is already at its target (the new layout) does not move.
- A result whose call was removed by `Compacted` stays where it is (today's behaviour).
- A result removed by `Compacted` while its call stays: the call keeps no result, as
  today.

**Step 5: correct the text of a moved late result.** If a moved result has exactly
the synthetic cancel text (`tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)`), the
repair replaces it with the G1 text: `transferred to {to}` for the first transfer call
of the response (`to` comes from the `HandoffOccurred` event), and `transfer not
performed: this response already transferred to {to}` for each other call. The
`HandoffOccurred` event proves that the transfer occurred, so the cancel text is false.
Without this step, the model sees "did not complete" after a transfer that succeeded,
and it can call the transfer tool again. A result with any other text keeps its text.

Properties:

- A log that has no `HandoffOccurred`, and a new-layout log, project exactly as today.
  This includes `ParallelAgent` logs with repeated ids.
- The repair adds and removes no message, so the message count stays the same.
  (`CompactingSession` counts tokens and checks `len()`; neither changes.)
- After the repair, a transfer call and its result are adjacent in the sense of
  `close_open_transfers` (result directly after the transfer calls of its response). So
  FIFO (`paired_result`, `agent_view`) and the step 2 rule give the same pairs for
  transfer calls. `close_open_transfers` keeps its "move" branch as a defence for a
  custom `Session` that overrides `snapshot()` without `project()`.
- `agent_view` (`deferral.rs`) calls `project()` per log segment. A segment that does
  not contain the `HandoffOccurred` of a transfer call does not move that call's result.
  The child segment drops the leading transfer result as today (it closes no open call).
- `ResumePlan::from_events` never maps snapshot indices to event indices. The repair
  moves results only to earlier positions and never reorders `ToolCall` items, so
  `CallNotInHistory` and `nth(later_calls)` keep their answers.
- `project()` emits one `tracing::debug!` (target `paigasus::core::session`) with the
  number of moved results when the number is not zero.
- The rustdoc of `project` states the repair, and that the snapshot order no longer
  follows the event order one-to-one for old-layout handoff logs.

Two spec challenges shaped this section. The first showed that removing state at
`ToolOutputItem` is not enough, and that two spans with one `toolCallId` break the
mapper's own client contract ("one call id maps to exactly one span", module doc). The
second showed that a reset at `TurnStarted` makes `ParallelAgent` output worse for every
provider: a sibling branch's `TurnStarted` can arrive between a call's deltas and its
`ToolCallItem`, and a reset there splits one call into two or renders it as `"unknown"`.
So G5 has **no reset at `TurnStarted`**. It starts a new occurrence of a provider id
only when the events prove that a new call started.

**Call occurrences.** The mapper keys all per-call state (`call_names`,
`completed_calls`, `buffered_calls`, `open_call`) by the **AG-UI id** of the occurrence,
not by the provider id. It keeps:

- `current: HashMap<String, Occurrence>`: provider id → the latest occurrence (its
  AG-UI id, whether a name-carrying delta was seen, whether its `ToolCallItem` was seen).
- `used_ids: HashSet<String>`: every AG-UI id that the run already emitted.

A new occurrence of provider id `x` starts when:

1. a `ToolCallDelta` for `x` with `name: Some(..)` arrives, and the current occurrence
   of `x` already had a name-carrying delta (the core contract gives `name: Some`
   exactly once per call, `model.rs`; the mapper already relies on this);
2. a `ToolCallItem` for `x` arrives, and the current occurrence of `x` already had its
   `ToolCallItem` (a non-streamed call that reuses the id);
3. there is no current occurrence of `x`.

`x~n` with the smallest `n` ≥ 2 such that `x~n` is not in `used_ids` (so an alias never
equals a provider id that the run already emitted). Every frame for the call (`START`,
`ARGS`, `END`, `RESULT`) uses the AG-UI id.

occurrence of `x`. A `helikon.approval` CUSTOM frame (`ApprovalRequested`) also maps its

content.text:
## Re-challenge result

**Verdict: approve with changes. There are no blockers.** The challenger traced the reworked G4 on all the sequential logs that I listed, and each result paired with its true call. The new position is valid for OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, LiteLLM and Bedrock.

**Changes I made from the findings:**

- **G5, new rule.** A reset at `TurnStarted` makes `ParallelAgent` output worse for every provider, including OpenAI and Anthropic. So there is no reset now. A new call occurrence starts only when the events prove that a new call started:
  - a second name-carrying delta for the same id, or
  - a second `ToolCallItem` for the same id.

  With unique provider ids, the output is exactly as today.
- **G5, other changes:**
  - An alias never equals an id that the run already emitted.
  - The approval frame also uses the alias.
  - The spec now defines how the test oracle `assert_tool_calls_well_formed` changes. Without that definition, the oracle cannot pass on a correct implementation.
- **G4, text changes:**
  - I corrected the claim of why "transferred" is true. A result moves only when an event from the target lies between the handoff and the result.
  - I listed two exceptions where an old log keeps the cancel text.
  - The scan is exact only for sequential logs, the same limit as G3.
  - The cancel text becomes one shared constant.
- **Tests:** I added these cases:
  - a failed old `run()` keeps the cancel text;
  - a running child call keeps its own cancel text;
  - each level gets its own target name;
  - a `Compacted` event before the handoff;
  - a custom `Session` test that keeps coverage of the `close_open_transfers` move;
  - a `ParallelAgent` case that must give exactly today's output.

**New release constraint.** Until SMA-819 ships, the Anthropic translator sends `tool_result` before `tool_use` for the new handoff shape. The old shape was probably accepted, because the Anthropic API merges adjacent same-role turns. Neither the challenger nor I checked the old shape against the live API. If the old shape is accepted, SMA-810 would break Anthropic handoff sessions that work today. So the spec now says: merge the SMA-810 PR only after SMA-819 is merged, and state this in the PR body.

Do you approve this version and the release order? If you do, I start Stage 3 (the implementation plan).
